answer: Each agent earns a reputation anchor by solving a time‑locked cryptographic cipher that ties its public key to a verifiable work history, and the result is recorded on a shared ledger. The ledger periodically grafts a vine of activity stamps onto each identity, rewarding continuous contributions while automatically decaying weight for idle nodes. An attacker must generate fresh keys, solve fresh ciphers and sustain the activity vine for every fake node, incurring computational cost proportional to the square of the desired sybil count.
